questions.q: Put these in the order a single sales order typically moves through them.
options: Order Management, Shipping, Receivables, Cash Management
Receivables, Order Management, Shipping, Cash Management
Shipping, Cash Management, Order Management, Receivables
Cash Management, Receivables, Shipping, Order Management
questions.explain: The order is captured in Order Management, fulfilled by Shipping, billed by Receivables, then collected by Cash Management.

questions.q: What is the net order total for SO-48217 after the volume discount?
questions.explain: $58,000.00 list total minus a 5% ($2,900.00) volume discount equals $55,100.00 net.

questions.q: Who is typically responsible for the order validation stage (credit checks and approvals)?
options: Credit and collections analysts, sometimes with manager approval
Warehouse staff
The customer themselves
The General Ledger accountant
questions.explain: Credit and collections analysts, often alongside an Approval Management (AME) rule, own the validation stage.

questions.q: What are the two levels that make up every sales order?
options: Price list and tax code
Header and lines
Invoice and receipt
Hold and release
questions.explain: A sales order has a header (order-wide data) and one or more lines (item-specific data, each with its own status).

questions.q: What generally determines how much flexibility exists to change an order line?
options: The customer's industry
The day of the week the order was entered
How far the line has progressed through fulfillment
The number of lines on the order
questions.explain: The further a line has progressed — picked, shipped, invoiced — the fewer clean changes remain available.

questions.q: What is a price list in Oracle Fusion Order Management?
options: A list of customers eligible to place orders
A list of items on credit hold
A defined set of prices for items, usually by currency and sometimes customer segment
A report of shipped orders
questions.explain: A price list defines item prices, typically segmented by currency and sometimes by customer group.

questions.q: Why do the order and the ship-from warehouse need to agree?
options: Because only one warehouse can exist per company
Because warehouses and orders are stored in different currencies
Because inventory for a specific item must actually exist in the referenced inventory organization for the line to fulfill from there
Agreement is not actually required
questions.explain: The order references a specific ship-from organization, and inventory for that item must exist there for fulfillment to proceed.

questions.q: Why does the RMA need to reference the original sales order (SO-48217) directly?
options: It doesn't need to — RMAs are always standalone
So the customer's credit limit can be reduced
So the system can later connect the return to the correct invoice for an accurate credit
So the warehouse address can be changed
questions.explain: Referencing the original order is what allows the return to later connect to the right invoice and generate an accurate credit memo.

questions.q: What does confirming a shipment finalize?
options: The customer's credit limit
The General Ledger period close
The actual shipped quantity against the delivery
The item's list price
questions.explain: Ship confirmation locks in the actual quantity that shipped, which can differ from what was planned.

questions.q: What does AutoInvoice do with the data in the Receivables interface tables?
options: Reads it, validates it against Receivables setup, and creates real transactions for records that pass
Deletes it automatically after 24 hours
Sends it back to Order Management unchanged
Applies it directly as a cash receipt
questions.explain: AutoInvoice validates staged records and converts the ones that pass into actual Receivables transactions.

questions.q: What tool is used to investigate and correct rejected or errored AutoInvoice records?
options: Approval Management (AME)
Manage AutoInvoice Lines
Lockbox processing
Create Accounting
questions.explain: Manage AutoInvoice Lines lets users search, review reasons, correct, flag, and resubmit interface records.

questions.q: What is Harborview's open balance on SO-48217's invoice after the credit memo is applied?
What generates these journal entries in Oracle Fusion?
options: A person manually typing debits and credits for every transaction
Subledger Accounting rules reacting automatically to Receivables business events
The customer's own accounting system
A random number generator
questions.explain: Subledger Accounting (SLA) rules automatically generate the appropriate journal entries for each defined business event.

questions.q: What is SO-48217's open balance after the credit memo, and its terms?
options: $58,000.00, Due on receipt
questions.explain: After the $2,755.00 credit memo, the invoice balance is $52,345.00, due Net 30.

questions.q: Why can a transaction's accounting be complete in Receivables before it's visible in the General Ledger?
options: Because Receivables and GL use entirely separate charts of accounts
Because Receivables transactions never actually post
Because GL only updates once per year
Because transfer and posting to GL can be batched at defined intervals rather than happening immediately
questions.explain: Transfer and posting can run on a schedule separate from when the subledger accounting itself was finalized.

questions.q: What triggered SO-48217's credit check hold in Chapter 2?
options: Harborview was a brand-new, unverified customer
The item was out of stock
The order's size, combined with Harborview's existing open balance
The ship-to address was missing
questions.explain: The order's value combined with Harborview's open balance failed the automatic credit check at submission.

questions.q: What is the first step in this lesson's troubleshooting checklist?
options: Assume the General Ledger is wrong
Cancel the transaction immediately
Identify what stage the transaction is actually in, by checking its status rather than assuming
Contact the customer's bank
questions.explain: The checklist starts by confirming the transaction's actual current stage/status rather than assuming where it should be.

questions.q: What is the correct way to handle a customer's duplicate payment on the same invoice?
options: Delete the second receipt entirely since it wasn't needed
Retain it as an on-account credit for future use, or refund it — never simply delete it
Apply it to a completely unrelated customer's account
Ignore it; it will resolve itself
questions.explain: Real cash arrived and must be accounted for — as an on-account credit or a refund, not deleted.
